transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, hi. I guess… work is the main reason I’m here. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m careless or anything, because I really do try, but I’ve been forgetting scheduled callbacks and work orders, and then little follow-ups I told people I’d handle just… don’t get done.

It’s kind of piled up, honestly. My job sent me here because it’s starting to affect things, and I’m worried I could lose my chance to move up if I don’t get a handle on it. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

I mean… not really, I don’t think. I get frustrated and embarrassed about the work stuff, sure, but I wouldn’t say I feel hopeless or like I’ve stopped caring about things. At least, not in that way. Is that what you mean?
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks or conversations, or do you get easily distracted by things around you?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not trying to pay attention, because I am. But with the digital work orders, I’ll start reading the notes thinking, okay, I’ve got this, and then halfway through my mind kind of slips off—like to another noise nearby or the next job I’m worried about.

Then I’ll look back and realize I don’t actually know what I just read. It’s embarrassing, but that does happen.
Do these difficulties with focus and forgetfulness happen only at work, or do they also occur in other parts of your life, like at home or with friends?

Mostly it’s been showing up at work, or at least that’s where it’s causing the biggest problem. I mean, I’m sure I forget little things other places too, like anybody does, but what brought me in is the scheduled callbacks, the work orders, and even basic follow-ups I told people I’d take care of… and then I just don’t.

It’s gotten piled up enough that my job sent me here, and I’m trying to fix it before it costs me my chance to move up. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
When did you first notice these issues with focus and forgetfulness? Were they happening even before this current job pressure started building up?

I guess… if I’m being honest, it wasn’t just this job. I remember being kind of like this even back in grade school, though I hate making it sound like an excuse.

Teachers would say I was bright, but I was always misplacing papers or missing part of the directions. I’d need reminders to finish classwork, that kind of thing. I think I just learned to work around it as best I could, so I didn’t really call it a problem until now. Does that make sense?
Do you also notice these same kinds of attention and forgetfulness issues outside of work, like at home or when you’re with friends or family?

Um… I guess I notice it some outside of work, but honestly the big thing—the reason I’m here—is work. I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, or I’ll miss something in a work order, or I’ll tell somebody I’ll follow up and then it just… doesn’t happen.

I don’t mean to make it sound like I don’t care, because I really do. It’s just piled up enough now that they sent me here, and I’m worried it could mess up my chance to move up if I don’t get it under control. Does that answer what you mean?
Can you think of any situations outside of work—like at home, while running errands, or spending time with friends—where you’ve noticed the same kind of trouble staying focused or forgetting things?

I mean… I’m sure there are little things outside of work too, but the main thing I can clearly point to is still work. That’s where it’s really catching up with me.

I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, or missing pieces of work orders, and sometimes I’ll tell someone I’ll follow up and then I just… don’t remember to do it until it’s already become a problem. I’m not trying to be careless. It’s just piled up enough now that work sent me here, and I really don’t want it to cost me my chance to move up. Is that the kind of example you mean?
Can you think of a specific situation at home or with friends where you noticed the same kind of trouble staying focused or forgetting things, even if it wasn't as serious as at work?

I’m trying to think of a good example… and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

Nothing really jumps out the way the work stuff does. At home, if something happens, I usually just kind of catch it or work around it, so I don’t know if I’d call it the same thing. With friends, I can’t think of a specific time right now.

Is it okay if I say I’m not really sure? The work examples are just much clearer to me.
Can you remember if these focus and forgetfulness issues happen in other places, like when you're at home doing something important or trying to follow a conversation with someone close to you?

I’m honestly not sure. I mean, at home I probably have moments where I lose track of what I was doing, but I can’t think of one clear example that feels important enough to point to.

With conversations… I don’t know, I haven’t really had someone close to me complain about it or anything. The work stuff is just so much more obvious to me. I’m sorry if that’s not the kind of answer you’re looking for.

When you're at home trying to focus on something important, like a chore or a task you need to get done, do you find yourself getting distracted or losing track of what you're doing in a way that feels similar to what you've described at work?

Yeah… I guess it does happen, maybe not as obvious to me at home.

Like when I’m trying to look at a digital work order, I’ll start reading it thinking, okay, I’ve got this, and then halfway through the notes my mind kind of slips off—like to the next noise or the next job I’m thinking about—and then I realize I don’t actually know what I just read.

So… yes, I think that’s similar. I don’t mean to make excuses, but it’s like I’m looking right at it and still not taking it in. Is that what you mean?
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or as though you’re constantly on the go, even when you’re trying to relax or focus on a task?

I don’t think so… not in a big way, anyway.

I mean, I might shift around or get up if I’m uncomfortable, but I wouldn’t say I feel like I’m constantly on the go or anything like that. When I’m trying to relax, I’m usually able to sit there. At least, I haven’t really noticed restlessness as a main problem.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had periods where you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had bad days, like anyone, where I’m tired or discouraged, but I can’t really remember a stretch where it was most of the day, every day, for two weeks like that.

At least nothing that stands out to me that way. Is that helpful?
Looking back, do you think these issues with attention and forgetfulness have been a consistent part of your life since childhood, or have they gotten noticeably worse only recently?

I think it’s been there a long time, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but… yeah, even back in grade school I remember being kind of like this.

Teachers would say I was bright, but I’d lose papers all the time, or I’d miss part of the directions and then not know what I was supposed to be doing. I needed reminders to finish classwork. So I don’t think it’s only just recently because of job pressure, even if it feels more obvious now. Does that answer what you’re asking?
